source_snapshot.procedure: Run `openbmctool.py <connection options> ldap disable` after generic prechecks/log clearing.
source_snapshot.criteria: The command succeeds and response is HTTP 200. The note requires root enabled before the action because otherwise BMC access may be lost, references phosphor-user-manager and says openbmctool cannot enable one specific user.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes that disabling LDAP removes an authentication path but exposes credentials in a URL-like connection example, treats HTTP 200 as removal proof, assumes root can be enabled and does not establish the resulting configuration, mapping, CA or active-session state.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with CRITICAL risk correctly requires a pinned supported action, complete auth/account/session baseline, independently verified local recovery, one disable, full policy readback, new-LDAP denial, local-admin verification and no blind root enablement.

old_problem: The title says Delete while the command is named `ldap disable`; the earlier review therefore left an engineer decision over object deletion versus disable-with-retained-state. HTTP 200 does not identify which LDAP fields, CA trust, privilege mappings or sessions changed, and the source root note can cause a second unsafe account mutation if followed blindly.
disposition_reason: Upstream openbmctool documentation explicitly names `ldap disable` as its `Delete/Erase LDAP Configuration` operation, reconciling the source title and Procedure for this named tool. The Review layer preserves that exact operation, requires a target-version post-state contract and independent readback for configuration, CA, mappings and sessions, and never infers deletion from HTTP 200. Platform-specific persistence/session values are Project configuration requirements; an unverified value makes execution NOT READY, not the review Engineering Decision Pending.
decision_basis: XLSX row 929, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, adjacent Create/Add-Mapping rows and the preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed; row 930 and its manifest identity were independently verified.

Pinned upstream openbmctool documentation labels the documented `ldap disable` command as `Delete/Erase LDAP Configuration`; this is direct evidence that the command is the intended implementation of the title, not an unrelated substitute.

The same documentation separately exposes LDAP root-certificate deletion and privilege-mapper deletion commands. Therefore this case must inventory CA and mappings but must not claim that `ldap disable` deletes those separate artifacts unless target readback proves the approved expected post-state.

OpenBMC user-management architecture distinguishes local and LDAP PAM authentication. The source root-access requirement is retained as a precondition, but enabling root/local users is a separate security change and cannot be performed implicitly.

test_case.test_name: Execute the documented openbmctool LDAP Delete/Erase action once and prove exact authentication post-state
test_case.purpose: Verify that one approved pinned `openbmctool ldap disable` performs the documented Delete/Erase LDAP Configuration operation on the intended BMC, prevents new LDAP authentication, leaves the exact firmware-approved configuration/CA/mapping/session post-state, preserves an independently proven local root recovery path, and can be restored through a separately approved complete configuration action.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware identity and pinned reviewed openbmctool/openbmc-tools commit whose LDAP disable semantics are supported
Complete redacted pre-state of LDAP mode/URI/DNs/scope/type, CA fingerprints, privilege mappings, local-user status, authentication policy and active sessions
Target-version authority binding whether the LDAP object is absent or disabled after Delete/Erase, whether CA/mappings persist, and how existing LDAP sessions must behave
Already-enabled and independently tested local root account as required by the source, protected credential path and independent console/recovery access
Named disposable LDAP identity for new-login denial plus approved active-session test identities where session behavior is in scope
Point-of-action approval for one delete/disable, protected BMC credential handling and a separately approved complete restore/recreate payload
test_case.test_command: CRITICAL AUTHENTICATION-PATH REMOVAL; DO NOT EXECUTE WITHOUT APPROVAL. Preserve security logs and capture the complete redacted LDAP/auth/CA/mapping/account/session baseline. Pin/review the tool and exact target semantics. Prove the source-required local root account is already enabled and usable from an independent session and that console recovery works; if root is disabled, stop and handle any enablement as a separate approved testcase/change rather than using `local_users enableall` implicitly. Bind the expected post-state matrix for config object or enabled flag, CA, mappings and existing sessions from target documentation/Project policy. After point-of-action approval, run exactly one protected `openbmctool ldap disable`, capture redacted response/audit, then independently read every matrix element. Prove a new disposable LDAP login is denied, existing-session behavior matches the approved policy, and local root login/role remains valid. Restore/recreate only with separate approval and the complete saved payload. Never clear logs, terminate unrelated sessions, expose credentials or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: The pinned tool issues one successful documented Delete/Erase action and the target readback matches the pre-authorized post-state matrix: LDAP is not available for new authentication; its object/Enabled state, CA trust and privilege mappings are exactly absent or retained as target documentation requires; existing LDAP sessions follow the approved revoke/retain behavior; and independently tested local root administration remains available. Audit evidence is preserved. Any restore recreates the exact approved configuration only through a separate change and restores expected LDAP/local access.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the pinned action, HTTP response plus audit event, exact configuration/CA/mapping/session readback against a pre-bound authoritative matrix, new-LDAP denial, successful source-required local root login/role and approved restore/final-state proof. HTTP 200 alone cannot pass. Continued new LDAP access, unexpected retained/deleted artifacts, unexpected session survival/termination, root/local lockout, wrong target, secret exposure, partial state or inability to restore is FAIL and stops. Missing target semantics, an already usable local root path, recovery, approval or restore payload is NOT READY. An alternative local admin may be a separately approved bounded override but must record the unsatisfied root-specific source coverage.
safety_gate: Do not run if LDAP is the only verified administrative path. Prove local root and independent console recovery before any authentication change.
Do not use `local_users enableall`, blindly enable root, change protected accounts or terminate sessions as an implicit prerequisite; each is a separate approved security action.
Protect BMC credentials using the documented prompt/protected environment path and keep them out of URLs, command history, process listings, logs and screenshots.
Bind exact expected post-state for configuration, CA, mappings and sessions before execution; do not infer deletion from tool name or HTTP status.
Execute once only. Stop on timeout, partial state, continued LDAP access, unexpected artifact/session change or local-access impact; preserve logs and recover through console without blind retry.
expected_evidence: Approved target/change, firmware, pinned tool commit/hash and target-version Delete/Erase post-state authority
Complete redacted pre-state for LDAP config, CA fingerprints, mappings, local/root accounts, auth policy and named active sessions
Independent local root login/role and console-recovery proof before the action, with no bulk account enablement
One protected disable response, HTTP status, security audit event and independent config/Enabled/CA/mapping post-readback
New disposable LDAP-login denial, approved existing-session behavior and continued local root login/role evidence
Separate restore/recreate approval and final equality/access proof, or explicitly approved retained post-state, with preserved logs and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On timeout, partial deletion/disablement, unexpected CA/mapping/session behavior or loss of local access, stop without another write. Use the independent console/recovery path, preserve security logs, restore the complete saved LDAP/auth policy only through its separately approved create/CA/mapping steps, verify local access first and then LDAP behavior. Do not bulk-enable users or claim recovery until full state equality is proven.

source_conflict.reason: The authoritative documentation for the source-named tool explicitly places `ldap disable` under `Delete/Erase LDAP Configuration`, establishing that the title and command describe the same tool operation. Exact artifact/session effects remain an explicit target post-state matrix rather than an invented universal behavior.

blocked.reason: The operation, evidence model, safety boundary and recovery are defined. Firmware-specific artifact/session persistence and credentials are execution inputs that can be bound before running.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Target firmware/tool commit; authoritative config/CA/mapping/session post-state matrix; complete baseline; already enabled root/local recovery; protected credentials; disposable identities; one-action and restore approvals.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; CRITICAL AUTHENTICATION-PATH REMOVAL; POINT-OF-ACTION APPROVAL REQUIRED; NO LDAP OR LOCAL-USER STATE CHANGED
